member_findings.reasoning: Hypothesis: a low-privileged BackWPup role can abuse '/getblock' to load admin-only partials that expose stored secrets. Trace: the route registers 'getblock' with permission_callback 'has_permission()', and that callback only checks current_user_can('backwpup') [src/Frontend/API/Rest.php:50-67]. The shipped 'backwpup_check' role has 'backwpup=true' but not 'backwpup_jobs_edit' or 'backwpup_settings' [inc/class-install.php:142-177]. Plugin admin pages localize both the REST URLs and a valid 'wp_rest' nonce to BackWPup users [inc/class-admin.php:1225-1254]. Inside getblock(), attacker-controlled 'block_type' may be 'children' and attacker-controlled 'block_name' is passed to BackWPupHelpersAdapter::children() [src/Frontend/API/Rest.php:91-99]; the helper only blocks traversal and then includes any file under 'parts/' [inc/Utils/BackWPupHelpers.php:72-109]. Requesting 'block_name=sidebar/storage-FTP' returns a form whose password field is prefilled with BackWPup_Encryption::decrypt( BackWPup_Option::get( $job_id, 'ftppass' ) ) [parts/sidebar/storage-FTP.php:170-179]. The same route can expose decrypted S3, MS Azure, and Rackspace credentials and the external job auth key [parts/sidebar/storage-S3.php:229-244, parts/sidebar/storage-MSAZURE.php:74-79, parts/sidebar/storage-RSC.php:92-99, parts/sidebar/settings-jobs.php:61-70]. Defenses analyzed/refutation: getblock() constrains block_type to 'component' or 'children' and the helper blocks path traversal [src/Frontend/API/Rest.php:91-99; inc/Utils/BackWPupHelpers.php:74-97], but there is no allowlist or secondary capability check for secret-bearing partials. The normal settings and edit pages are separately gated by 'backwpup_settings' and 'backwpup_jobs_edit' [inc/class-page-settings.php:419-420; inc/class-page-editjob.php:45-49], so the REST helper bypasses the intended privilege split. Conclusion: CONFIRMED sensitive data exposure to low-privileged BackWPup roles.
member_findings.remediation: Restrict '/getblock' to an allowlist of safe partials and require route-specific capabilities such as 'backwpup_jobs_edit' or 'backwpup_settings' before rendering secret-bearing admin blocks.

phase3_review.reason: The /getblock REST route at src/Frontend/API/Rest.php:83 uses has_permission() checking only current_user_can(backwpup) (line 50-67). The getblock() handler dispatches attacker-controlled block_name via BackWPupHelpersAdapter::children() to partials under parts/. Requesting block_name=sidebar/storage-FTP returns parts/sidebar/storage-FTP.php which prefills a password field with BackWPup_Encryption::decrypt(BackWPup_Option::get(job_id, ftppass)). Same pattern exposes S3, Azure, Rackspace, SugarSync credentials. The backwpup_check role (backwpup=true, no backwpup_settings) can obtain decrypted cloud credentials for all jobs. Gate path_reachability failure and guard_contradiction are false negatives — both confirmed absent.

counter_evidence.detail: block_type constrained to ['component','children'] — no arbitrary type injection.
realpath() + directory boundary check blocks path traversal outside parts/ directory.

missing_evidence: Whether the wp_rest nonce is emitted to backwpup_check users via get_backwpup_api_data() — confirmed accessible since it requires only current_user_can(backwpup).
Whether job_id is validated against jobs the caller owns — if not, any job's credentials are readable.

Step 3: POST /wp-json/backwpup/v1/getblock with X-WP-Nonce header. Body: {"block_name":"sidebar/storage-FTP","block_type":"children","block_data":{"job_id":1}}
